history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, temple, or business-directory source documents a specific 'Ganesha Temple' in Williamnagar; the identity, exact location, age, and history of this shrine could not be verified from web or social sources, so this entry is provisional (verify - confirm on the ground in Williamnagar before any further publication). Williamnagar is the planned district headquarters town of East Garo Hills on the Simsang plain, named after Captain Williamson A. Sangma, Meghalaya's first chief minister; the area is historically noted for the Garos' last major resistance to the British in 1837 (legendary leader Pa Togan Nengminja Sangma fell at Chisobibra, 12 December 1837). The Garo Hills are today overwhelmingly Christian, and Hindu shrines in the region are generally small, community-serving temples of the non-tribal population (Bengali, Nepali, Assamese, Hindi-speaking) rather than historic pilgrimage sites. Do not conflate this entry with Ganesha temples in Assam (Goalpara, Kamrup) or elsewhere that surfaced in searches.

town_description: Williamnagar is the headquarters of East Garo Hills district, Meghalaya, a planned town on the Simsang (Simsanggre) plain named after Captain Williamson A. Sangma, the state's first chief minister. It stands about 313 km from Shillong and 76 km from Tura, in historically significant country where the Garos made their last major resistance to British intrusion in 1837. Nearby attractions include the Simsang river, Rongbang Dare waterfall and the Nokrek and Balphakram national parks further afield.
